explains: A new handler get_invoice_pdf is appended to services/billing/app/routers/invoices.py, declared with @router.get("/{invoice_id}/pdf"). Every added line is placed by diff line number, so every changed line is inside get_invoice_pdf. Its parameter line (    request: Request,) is textually identical to the parameter line of list_invoices, get_invoice and void_invoice in the same file (and of every handler in the other routers), so placing lines by their text would mark all of them changed; none of them is. Route: /api + /billing + /invoices + /{invoice_id}/pdf = GET /api/billing/invoices/{invoice_id}/pdf. It is a new route that no web URL reaches (invoiceUrl ends at the invoice id; nothing builds a /pdf URL), so no http edge and no screen is claimed. An added route nobody calls yet is said: the finding added_route_uncalled cites the new decorator line (low risk, since nothing depends on the route yet; medium confidence, since only the web client in this workspace was read).

must_exclude.why: shares the parameter line request: Request, with the new handler; its own lines are unchanged
